title: MODE 5 ▶ 3: AB-Exp
summary: Enter x , y DT pairs (≥2, y > 0), AC, then recall A, B, and r. Fitted curve: y = A B^x. Distinct from Exp (y = A e^(Bx)).

body.text: AB-Exp fits y = A B^x (same as y = A · B^x). Each equal step in x multiplies y by the same base B — geometric / discrete compound growth. This is a different parametrisation from Exp (y = A e^(Bx)): here B is the multiplier itself, not the coefficient in the exponent. The same curve family is related by B_AB = e^b if Exp’s coefficient is b.

AB-Exp fits y = A B^x. Each equal step in x multiplies y by the same base B — geometric growth. This is not the same recall as Exp (y = A e^(Bx)): here B is the multiplier itself. Same curve family: AB-Exp’s B equals e^b if Exp’s coefficient is b.

body.caption: Sample fit y = 2 × 1.5^x. Compare with Exp: here the multiplier is B itself, not e^B.

body.text: Open AB-Exp regression (MODE 5, ▶, then 3), clear old data, enter at least two pairs as x , y DT. y values must be positive (the model uses ln y internally). The fitted base B is typically positive.
